analysis.title: Midterms - Macro view + replay
key_insights: Aggressive bid across markets after the midterms. Trump told the NYT he would accept the election results, which removed some left tail risk. Crude fell 8% and Brent went back to about $95, through the $100 level, which renewed an index-level bid.

GS macro (Hatzius): Democrats won the House and Senate by larger-than-expected majorities. This gives them somewhat more leverage with the White House and dilutes the influence of small factions inside their caucus.

GS expects Democrats to use fiscal deadlines to seek limits on the war with Iran, selected tariff rollbacks and a reversal of last year's spending cuts. Expanded health benefits also appear high on their list.

Senate: media outlets have called seven Republican-held seats for Democrats (Iowa, Kansas, North Carolina, Ohio, South Carolina, Maine, Texas). Alaska is not yet called but is implied likely by prediction markets, and Mississippi may take days. Winning both would give Democrats 56 seats.

House: a Democratic majority has been called, with a popular vote margin likely D+12-14. That is consistent with a majority of around 255 seats. The final size could take days because of California counting.

Fiscal: reversing last year's spending cuts would add about 0.25% of GDP to spending in 2027. The first test is December 11, when spending authority expires. A short-term extension to February or March is the base case, though Democrats could try to extract concessions before taking control. Results generally take effect January 3, 2027, and the Ohio Senate special on December 15.
The federal outcome is less likely to change AI and data center regulation, since passage would still need bipartisan Senate support and would face a veto.

State and local wins matter more for data centers. Republicans lost governorships in Texas, Ohio, Nevada, Georgia and Michigan, and Democrats gained a trifecta in Pennsylvania and likely Arizona. GS expects conditional moratoria in Texas, Georgia and Michigan pending new legislation.

States likely to restrict data centers account for about 45% of planned US data center capacity expansion, with Texas alone near 25%. GS equity analysts see a possible negative for select US utilities and independent power producers. GS expects the issue to fade in importance and any moratoria to be short-lived.
Oil: the risk premium has fallen sharply, but GS still sees downside risks to Middle East supply. It raised its average 2027 Brent forecast to $88/bbl from $80/bbl, and raised its 2027 TTF forecasts.

Europe: the higher energy forecasts lead GS to expect weaker growth and higher inflation next year. 2027 growth is now 0.9% (was 1.3%), with peak core inflation of 2.9% (was 2.7%) and peak headline of 4.1% (was 3.9%).

GS trader Flood: equity investors of all cohorts have had a tough stretch since July. Hedge fund net exposure is historically low and gross ticked lower last week. Long-only funds hold significant cash raised during the July and October selloffs and have mostly not redeployed it.

Flood: October is the largest fiscal year-end month for mutual funds, and the 10/30 session saw long-only selling tied to it. This set up the midterms as a clean positioning clearing event, but he sees the most critical clearing event of the year still ahead and tied to equity capital markets.

State-level data center moratoria could affect about 45% of planned US data center capacity expansion and hurt select utilities and independent power producers.
The December 11 spending authority expiry and the debt limit due by next fall are leverage points for Democrats and could produce standoffs.
An equity capital markets event is still ahead and is seen as the most critical clearing event for the market this year.

tension_points.bull_case: The oil risk premium has declined significantly as Democrats are expected to seek limits on the Iran war, and Brent fell back to about $95 from above $100.
tension_points.bear_case: Downside risks to Middle East oil supply could raise the risk premium again, and GS raised its 2027 Brent forecast to $88/bbl from $80/bbl.

tension_points.bull_case: Data centers rank low among voter priorities, so GS expects the issue to fade and any moratoria to be short-lived. Federal regulation is unlikely to change.
tension_points.bear_case: Democratic governors in Texas, Georgia and Michigan are expected to impose conditional moratoria. Legislation could end tax breaks and tighten environmental, water and electricity rules, which could hurt select utilities and independent power producers.
